## Notes

`[cost_basis]` next to a 0 cost, and `[hardware]` next to every latency figure, are generated from each run's `results/<run-name>.run_meta.json` -- not hand-typed.

**What a `[cost_basis]` tag means:**

- `api-per-token`: a hosted API call. The provider doesn't return a live $ figure per request, so a cost_usd of 0 here means UNMEASURED -- compute a real figure externally from the recorded input/output token counts -- not that the call was free.
- `cpu-local`: runs entirely on a local CPU. A cost_usd of 0 here is real and measured -- genuinely free to run, no ambiguity.

**Training cost** (a one-time cost, not part of any single prediction above -- so it is not, and cannot be, folded into `latency_ms` or `cost_usd`):

- (none of the runs above report GPU training hours)

Runs not listed above required no GPU training step of their own -- either a pre-trained hosted API model, or (TF-IDF, the random baseline) a fit measured in seconds of CPU time, not GPU-hours; see each such run's `training_cost.note` in `results/results.json` for the exact figure.

## Superseded runs (excluded from the comparison above)

Kept in `results/results.json` for this project's own methodology record -- NOT deleted -- but excluded from the table above because each one is a known-bad result, not a fair comparison point. Do not read these numbers as competitive with the runs above.

- **`api-gpt4o-mini-50`** (`test`, n=50): Known-bad sample, preserved intentionally (not deleted): all 50 tickets in this run share a single queue value, "Billing and Payments" -- the step-04 sampling-trap bug. This run used --limit 50 (df.head(50)) against test.parquet BEFORE step-04's shuffle fix, when a split's row order was grouped by queue class -- so "the first 50 rows" was a slice of one class, not a representative sample. Not comparable to any other run in this table. See PROGRESS.md's step-04 and step-17 entries. See `api-gpt4o-mini-full-test` instead.

## Next steps

- **Fine-tuning a hosted API model (e.g. OpenAI's `gpt-4o-mini` fine-tuning) was considered and
  deliberately not done.** The fine-tuning target is instead an open-weights 1-3B instruct model
  (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` by default -- see `FT_BASE_MODEL` in `.env.example`), QLoRA
  fine-tuned on Colab, so it can be self-hosted, quantized, and served in Docker in later steps.
  Fine-tuning a hosted API model instead would make those later steps meaningless and would kill
  the self-hosted-vs-API cost comparison this project is built around.
